# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 44 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_044_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 44

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever blasphemes [жіоуа] against the Father will be forgiven [ка евол], and whoever blasphemes against the Son will be forgiven.

**2** But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit [пна єтоуаав] will not be forgiven, either on earth [кахе] or in heaven [тпе]."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *жіоуа*: to blaspheme, curse, revile
- *ка евол*: to forgive, release; the compound verb means "put it outside"
- *пна єтоуаав*: Holy Spirit; literally "the holy breath/spirit"
- Thomas's version is notable: it differentiates three objects of blasphemy (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) with different consequences
- The unique element: blasphemy against the Father and the Son are forgivable; only against the Spirit is not
- cf. Matt 12:31-32; Mark 3:28-29; Luke 12:10 — the Synoptic unforgivable sin saying
- Matthew and Luke single out blasphemy against the Holy Spirit (vs. against the Son of Man); Thomas agrees but adds the Father as also forgivable

---
